title: Staged Sparse-Artifact Sync & Controlled Egress Policy for Private Deployments
creator: Asha Nair
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private in highly constrained networks (low bandwidth, intermittent egress windows, or fully air-gapped environments) need a deterministic, auditable way to receive only the minimal set of artifacts required for a runtime upgrade or bootstrap. Current mirror and full-image distribution approaches cause long upgrade windows, increased patch risk, and significant operator toil when networks are restricted.

Goal: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a staged 'sparse sync' mechanism plus a controlled egress policy that: (1) only transfers signed artifact subsets required for a specific deployment or upgrade plan, (2) supports incremental resume and chunked transfer over constrained links, (3) provides deterministic fallback to physical media or operator-assisted mirroring, and (4) integrates with our upgrade orchestration to keep SLOs and rollback paths intact.
scope:
In scope: artifact manifest format and signing, staged sync controller behavior, egress window policy integration, operator playbook for physical media fallback, integration tests for upgrades over bandwidth-limited links, and console UX for mirror plan visualization.
Out of scope: changes to customer-side airgap proxy implementations beyond documented configuration, deep changes to image build pipelines, and encrypted hardware transport (handled by separate KMS scope).
success_metrics: 1) Mean upgrade time reduction in limited-bandwidth (<=10 Mbps) environments by >=40% for minor patch releases. 2) Successful unattended staged upgrades in 95% of simulated intermittent-connect scenarios in CI. 3) Documented operator median time-to-recover < 30 minutes when staged-sync falls back to offline media. 4) No increase in CVE exposure window across supported versions.
constraints:
- Must conform to existing offline/airgap contractual constraints (no unsolicited egress).
- Signed artifacts only; compatibility with current image signing process required.
- No additional persistent outbound open ports beyond configured egress proxy patterns.
- Changes must be deployable via existing private-operator manifests without cluster-wide API changes.
technical_requirements:
- Artifact manifest format (JSON) listing minimal required layers/blobs, semantic tags, and delta references.
- Signed manifest using current KMS key rotation policy.
- Chunked transfer protocol over HTTPS with resumable offsets and exponential backoff.
- Optional rsync-like delta pull for layer deltas.
- On-device verification post-transfer: integrity (sha256), signature verification, and dry-run install validation.
- Console view for planned staged-sync that displays expected bytes and egress windows.
- Upgrade orchestrator extension to understand staged manifests and to perform canary-stage pulls before core rollout.
rollout_plan:
1) Design + spec review with Security and Infra (2 weeks). 2) Prototype staged manifest + transfer lib in a feature branch (3 weeks). 3) Internal integration tests with simulated 5Mbps/10Mbps/partitioned networks (2 weeks). 4) Beta with three enterprise customers with scheduled egress windows (6 weeks). 5) GA after fixes and security sign-off.
Fallback: If staged-sync fails in beta, enable operator-assisted physical media path with a verified checklist and provide a signed 'restore manifest' to ensure exact artifact set.
acceptance_criteria:
- AC1: Staged manifest schema published and signed by Redwood KMS; sample publisher script exists.
- AC2: Pull client can resume transfers and validate chunk integrity after simulated interruptions; unit/integration tests cover resume scenarios.
- AC3: Upgrades driven by staged manifests complete in <=60% of baseline time for 10Mbps test and succeed without manual intervention in 95% of test runs.
- AC4: Console shows estimated egress size for staged plan and flags any artifact requiring extra operator approval.
- AC5: Operator playbook for physical-media fallback exists and walk-through completed in dry-run with an internal staging cluster.
- AC6: Security review completed and threat-model updated to account for manifest replay and signature expiry.
- AC7: No new open egress ports beyond configured egress proxy; compliance audit passes for one beta customer site.
- AC8: Telemetry tracks staged-sync bytes, retries, resume occurrences, and final verification status; metrics ingested into console within retention window.
qa_steps:
- Simulate constrained link (5 Mbps) and run full staged upgrade; verify time and integrity.
- Inject mid-transfer network interruption; verify resume and checksum pass.
- Validate signature expiry behavior by using expired manifest and ensure client rejects install.
- Run canary staged-sync and then abort core rollout; verify nodes remain consistent and KV cache warmup not corrupted.
- Execute off-network physical-media fallback using a prepared manifest; verify install matches expected digest list.
risk_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Manifests become stale and cause partial installs. Mitigation: manifest has required precondition checks and dry-run verification step.
- Risk: Replay or downgrade attacks on manifests. Mitigation: signatures with nonces and strict server-side rotation checks.
- Risk: Operator confusion over staged vs full mirror. Mitigation: console UX with clear 'staged' badge, estimated bytes, and mandatory confirmation for >X MB operations.
- Risk: Increased engineering surface area. Mitigation: implement as an optional plugin for the operator with well-defined API contract.
notes: This approach is intentionally conservative: aim to minimize protocol surface while delivering measurable upgrade time reduction for constrained networks. The sparse-sync concept can later be adopted for deduped caching in Dedicated pools if successful.
